Corollary
[Ricci trace of the curvature quadratic] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-ii:page-0114, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-ii:page-0115 ↗ def:chow-ii-sharp-product ↗ def:chow-ii-algebraic-ricci-contraction 1. ch11:11.18\group Curvature Operator Algebra For $R\in \mathcal A_n$, one has $Q(R)\in \mathcal A_n$ and \[ \operatorname {Rc}(Q(R))_{ij} =\sum _{k,\ell }\operatorname {Rc}(R)_{k\ell }R_{ikj\ell }, \qquad \operatorname {Scal}(Q(R))=|\operatorname {Rc}(R)|^2. \] In particular, $\ker \operatorname {Rc}$ is invariant under $Q$.
Proof

\sketch Expanding $R^2+R^\# $ by the same component calculation as in 3 shows first that its cyclic Bianchi sum vanishes. Contracting its first and third indices, and then using the Bianchi identity $R_{aebf}R_{cdef}=\tfrac 12R_{abef}R_{cdef}$, gives the first displayed identity. Taking its trace gives the second. If $\operatorname {Rc}(R)=0$, the first identity vanishes.

□
